scientific_goal: Task-conditioned executable skill-parameter reinforcement learning with genuine physical execution-effect adaptation for transferable robotic manipulation
next_action: Repeat native PlugCharger strong controllers with matched resets and bounded planning randomness; attribute failure to planning/tracking/contact/budget; characterize whether legal feedback corrections have repeatable benefit. If geometry solves them, pivot task, not weaken baseline.

experiments.primary_claim: Distinguish control defects and nondeterminism from state-dependent contact failures.
Find physically useful, executable contact-phase corrections under full-task constraints.
Get well-trained same-authority residual RL, with full-cost baselines.
Isolate additional causal value of explicit action-effect feedback over equal-observation/history RL and strong planning.
After a reliable independent gain, test novel conditions, another contact mechanism and industrial adapter.

unresolved_questions: How many native PlugCharger failures survive a fully tuned strong baseline within 200 steps?
Do legal contact actions rescue failures repeatably, accounting for MPLib/RRT variability?
Does effect history add deployable information beyond privileged current state and a generic history encoder?
Can a mature residual SAC/PPO learn the correction at reasonable counted physical+offline data cost?
Are benefits novel versus Foresight, STAP, DAWN, SCOUT and simple replan/search?
safety: ARES-R read-only; no live robot commands; no restricted field data in public artifacts; sealed evaluations not used in method search.
completion_protocol: Update experiments/<card>, DECISIONS.md, EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md and this STATE.json together after material experimental evidence; keep paper claims unverified until independent gain+mechanism ablation.
